title: BlockingQueue implementations — ArrayBQ, LinkedBQ, PriorityBQ, SynchronousQueue, DelayQueue
shortTitle: BlockingQueue implementations — ArrayBQ, LinkedBQ, PriorityBQ, SynchronousQueue, DelayQueue

s1_definition.profdef: Five `BlockingQueue` implementations, each for a different use case: **ArrayBlockingQueue** — fixed-size array, ONE lock for both put/take, optional fairness. **LinkedBlockingQueue** — linked nodes, TWO separate locks (putLock + takeLock → concurrent put+take!), bounded or unbounded. **PriorityBlockingQueue** — unbounded, min-heap ordering (smallest/highest-priority first), no FIFO. **SynchronousQueue** — ZERO capacity! `put()` blocks until `take()` → direct handoff. **DelayQueue** — elements available only after their delay expires (scheduled tasks). Each serves a different pattern: bounded buffer (Array/Linked), priority processing (Priority), direct handoff (Synchronous), scheduled execution (Delay).
s1_definition.analogy: **ArrayBlockingQueue** = fixed-size waiting bench (10 seats). One guard controls both entry and exit. **LinkedBlockingQueue** = expanding rope line with TWO guards — one at entry, one at exit → customers enter and exit simultaneously! **PriorityBlockingQueue** = VIP line — highest priority served first, not FIFO. **SynchronousQueue** = direct counter — customer hands form DIRECTLY to teller. No waiting area. Must wait for a teller. **DelayQueue** = scheduled appointments — only called when appointment time arrives.
s1_definition.oneliner: Array: fixed, 1 lock, fair option. Linked: dynamic, 2 locks (concurrent put+take!). Priority: heap-ordered. Synchronous: 0 capacity, direct handoff. Delay: time-based release.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** Five `BlockingQueue` implementations, each for a different use case: **ArrayBlockingQueue** — fixed-size array, ONE lock for both put/take, optional fairness. **LinkedBlockingQueue** — linked nodes, TWO separate locks (putLock + takeLock → concurrent put+take!), bounded or unbounded. **PriorityBlockingQueue** — unbounded, min-heap ordering (smallest/highest-priority first), no FIFO. **SynchronousQueue** — ZERO capacity! `put()` blocks until `take()` → direct handoff. **DelayQueue** — elements available only after their delay expires (scheduled tasks). Each serves a different pattern: bounded buffer (Array/Linked), priority processing (Priority), direct handoff (Synchronous), scheduled execution (Delay).

**In simple words (banking analogy):** **ArrayBlockingQueue** = fixed-size waiting bench (10 seats). One guard controls both entry and exit. **LinkedBlockingQueue** = expanding rope line with TWO guards — one at entry, one at exit → customers enter and exit simultaneously! **PriorityBlockingQueue** = VIP line — highest priority served first, not FIFO. **SynchronousQueue** = direct counter — customer hands form DIRECTLY to teller. No waiting area. Must wait for a teller. **DelayQueue** = scheduled appointments — only called when appointment time arrives.

**One line to remember:** Array: fixed, 1 lock, fair option. Linked: dynamic, 2 locks (concurrent put+take!). Priority: heap-ordered. Synchronous: 0 capacity, direct handoff. Delay: time-based release.

sections.s3_banking: **Problem — The trade processing engine needed 3 different queue behaviors:** (1) Settlement queue: bounded, high-throughput producer-consumer → `LinkedBlockingQueue(10000)` (two locks for concurrent put+take). (2) High-value trade queue: process Rs.10Cr trades before Rs.1L → `PriorityBlockingQueue` (priority ordering). (3) Retry queue: failed trades retried after 30-second delay → `DelayQueue`. Each queue type matched to its use case.

sections.s5_journey:
**Step 1 (LinkedBQ).** Producer `put("item")` → acquires putLock → adds to tail. Consumer `take()` → acquires takeLock → removes from head. CONCURRENT! Different locks!

**Step 2 (PriorityBQ).** `put(100), put(10M), put(50K)`. `take()` → 100 (smallest). `take()` → 50K. `take()` → 10M. Heap-ordered, NOT FIFO!

**Step 3 (SynchronousQ).** Producer `put("X")` → BLOCKS. Consumer `take()` → receives "X" instantly. Direct handoff, zero buffering.

**Step 4 (DelayQ).** `put(task, 30s delay)`. `take()` → BLOCKS for 30 seconds. When delay expires → task released.
sections.s5b_flow:
```
  ═══ FIVE BlockingQueue IMPLEMENTATIONS ═══

  ArrayBlockingQueue(100):     [■■■■■■■...100■■] fixed array, 1 lock
  LinkedBlockingQueue(1000):   [→■→■→■→...→■] linked, 2 locks (PUT‖TAKE!)
  PriorityBlockingQueue:       [min-heap] priority order, unbounded
  SynchronousQueue:            [] zero capacity! Direct handoff!
  DelayQueue:                  [⏰30s][⏰60s] released when delay expires!

  ═══ DECISION ═══
  Bounded FIFO + fairness:      ArrayBlockingQueue
  High-throughput producer-consumer: LinkedBlockingQueue (2 locks!)
  Priority processing:          PriorityBlockingQueue
  Direct handoff (no buffering): SynchronousQueue
  Scheduled/delayed execution:   DelayQueue
```

sections.s5d_lld:
```
  ═══ LLD — BlockingQueue Internals ═══

  ┌─ ArrayBlockingQueue ──────────────────┐
  │  Object[] items (circular array)       │
  │  1 ReentrantLock (put AND take!)      │
  │  Condition notEmpty, notFull          │
  │  Fair option: FIFO for waiting threads│
  └────────────────────────────────────────┘

  ┌─ LinkedBlockingQueue ─────────────────┐
  │  Node<E> linked list                   │
  │  putLock (tail) + takeLock (head)     │  TWO locks!
  │  Condition notEmpty (takeLock)        │
  │  Condition notFull (putLock)          │
  │  put() and take() CONCURRENT!        │  higher throughput!
  └────────────────────────────────────────┘

  ┌─ PriorityBlockingQueue ───────────────┐
  │  Object[] (binary heap)                │
  │  1 ReentrantLock                       │
  │  poll() returns min/max (Comparator!)  │
  │  UNBOUNDED — put never blocks!         │
  └────────────────────────────────────────┘

  ┌─ SynchronousQueue ───────────────────┐
  │  No internal storage!                  │
  │  put() blocks until take() (rendezvous)│
  │  Used by newCachedThreadPool()         │
  └────────────────────────────────────────┘

  ┌─ DelayQueue ──────────────────────────┐
  │  PriorityQueue<Delayed> (by delay)    │
  │  take() blocks until getDelay() ≤ 0  │
  │  Scheduled tasks, retry with backoff  │
  └────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Five BlockingQueue implementations for different patterns. `ArrayBlockingQueue`: fixed-size array, one ReentrantLock (put and take share the lock), optional fairness — use for bounded buffer with fair ordering. `LinkedBlockingQueue`: linked nodes, TWO separate locks (putLock + takeLock) — put and take can run CONCURRENTLY → higher throughput — the default for ThreadPoolExecutor. `PriorityBlockingQueue`: unbounded min-heap, elements ordered by Comparator/Comparable — use for priority processing (highest-value trades first). `SynchronousQueue`: zero capacity, direct handoff — put blocks until take (rendezvous) — used by newCachedThreadPool(). `DelayQueue`: elements released only after their delay expires — use for scheduled retry, cache expiration.

The key differentiator: LinkedBlockingQueue's two-lock design enables concurrent put+take — critical for high-throughput producer-consumer. In banking: settlement queue (LinkedBQ — throughput), VIP trade queue (PriorityBQ — priority), retry queue (DelayQ — 30-second retry delay).
